paraphrase: Nāgeśa: speech at rest in the root centre (mūlādhāra), unmanifest, is parā; moved by breath and manifest at the navel it is paśyantī; in the heart, joined to the intellect, it is madhyamā — the sphoṭa that conveys meaning; issuing through the throat and mouth it is vaikharī, heard by others.
notes: The four levels are accepted here by a grammarian (Nāgeśa) though Bhartṛhari names three; section name recalled.
